definition: A romantic entanglement that has the feelings and vibes of a relationship but none of the labels, commitment, or clarity.
example: They've been texting every day, going on dates, and watching movies together for 4 months — but the moment she asked 'what are we?', he said 'I don't like labels.' That's a situationship.
how_it_feels: Warm and confusing. Like you're almost there but also somehow nowhere.
what_to_do: Have the DTR talk. If they dodge it repeatedly, that IS your answer. You deserve clarity.
indian_context: Very common in college scenes where 'official' feels too heavy, or where family pressure means dating must stay hidden.

definition: The pre-relationship phase where two people are getting to know each other, flirting, and figuring out if they want something more — but haven't officially started dating.
example: They DM every day, she sends him good morning texts, they FaceTime for hours — but they're 'just talking.'
how_it_feels: Exciting, anxious, and annoyingly undefined.
what_to_do: Enjoy it but set a mental deadline. If it stays undefined for 2–3 months with no movement, it's worth a gentle conversation.
indian_context: Common in DMs and Instagram before moving to WhatsApp — escalating platforms is its own ritual.

definition: The conversation where two people explicitly talk about what they are — are we dating? Are we exclusive? Are we just friends?
example: 'Hey, I really like spending time with you. I want to be clear about what we are. Are we dating exclusively?'
how_it_feels: Terrifying but necessary. Like ripping off a Band-Aid that's been on for three months.
what_to_do: Have it when you feel ready, not when anxiety forces you. Choose a calm, private moment. Be honest about what YOU want first.
indian_context: Often skipped because of fear of rejection or cultural awkwardness — but skipping it causes way more pain later.

definition: When someone overwhelms you with affection, attention, gifts, and intensity very early in a relationship — often to the point where it feels too much, too fast.
example: 'You're the only person who's ever understood me.' (Day 3). 'I think I'm falling for you.' (Day 5). 'I can't imagine life without you.' (Day 9).
how_it_feels: Intoxicating at first, then unsettling. Like eating too much sugar — it's sweet but then your stomach hurts.
what_to_do: Slow down. If someone genuinely likes you, they'll still like you in three weeks. Healthy love builds gradually.
indian_context: Can be confused with passion or 'filmy' romance, especially when we've grown up watching dramatic declarations of love.

definition: Cutting off all contact with someone you've been talking to or dating without any explanation.
example: They were texting every day. Then suddenly — nothing. No reply. Last seen two weeks ago. No explanation.
how_it_feels: Like disappearing mid-sentence. Confusing, humiliating, and weirdly hard to get closure from.
what_to_do: Give one short check-in message. If there's no response, your answer is the silence. Don't chase — you deserve someone who communicates.
indian_context: Common because confrontation feels scary. Many people ghost instead of having an awkward but honest goodbye.

definition: When someone gives you just enough attention — a like, a late-night text, a 'haha' — to keep you interested without any real commitment or intention.
example: She doesn't reply for days, then sends 'hey stranger 😊' when she's bored. No plans ever materialise.
how_it_feels: Like following a trail of crumbs that never leads to actual food.
what_to_do: Match their energy. Stop over-investing in someone who's giving you the bare minimum. You can like someone and still walk away.
indian_context: WhatsApp last-seen stalking turns breadcrumbing into an Olympic sport. One blue tick can ruin a whole Tuesday.

definition: Introducing your partner to your social media audience gradually and subtly — a hand in a photo, a vague story — without confirming anything.
example: She posts a story of two coffees. No tag, no mention. But everyone's asking 'who's the other cup for?' That's a soft launch.
how_it_feels: Exciting if you're the one doing it. A little sus if you're the one being half-hidden.
what_to_do: Have a conversation about social media visibility. Everyone has different comfort levels and that's okay — as long as you both agree.
indian_context: In India, going Insta-official is a BIG deal — especially when family follows you. Soft-launching is the safety valve.

definition: Going fully public with your relationship on social media — tagged photo, 'my boyfriend/girlfriend', the works.
example: She posts a photo with him, tagged, captioned 'my person ❤️'. Full rollout. No more ambiguity.
how_it_feels: Official. A milestone. Slightly terrifying if you weren't expecting it.
what_to_do: Discuss it before it happens. Make sure both people are comfortable being public. Surprise hard-launches can feel like pressure.
indian_context: A hard-launch on Instagram can travel faster than a family WhatsApp group. Think before you post.

definition: Keeping someone as a backup option — not letting them go but not pursuing them seriously either. You're on the bench while they play the field.
example: He only texts when his other plans fall through. She's interested but always last priority.
how_it_feels: Like being a substitute player who never gets on the pitch.
what_to_do: Notice the pattern. Are they consistently unavailable? Do plans always get cancelled? You deserve a starting spot, not the bench.

definition: When someone stops talking to you but continues to watch your Instagram stories, like your posts, and stay in your peripheral vision — without actually reaching out.
example: He ghosted her but still watches every story she posts within 5 minutes. She can see him. He's just… orbiting.
how_it_feels: Confusing. Like someone who left the party but is peeking through the window.
what_to_do: Don't read too much into it. Social media is passive. If they wanted to talk, they'd message. Restrict or remove them if it bothers you.
indian_context: Instagram story views have become a whole psychological phenomenon. The 'he viewed my story in 10 seconds' analysis is real.

definition: Like orbiting, but they actively interact with very old posts — liking a photo from 2 years ago, watching archived stories. They're haunting your digital past.
example: She liked a photo of his from 2022 at 2 AM. They haven't spoken in 8 months.
how_it_feels: Spooky. Like finding out someone's been reading your old diary.
what_to_do: It might be intentional (they miss you) or accidental (the algorithm betrayed them). One weird like isn't a signal. Wait for actual words.

definition: When someone who ghosted you comes back from the dead — usually with a casual 'hey' or 'I've been thinking about you' — as if nothing happened.
example: They ghosted him for 3 months. Then sent 'hey stranger, been a while 😊' with no acknowledgement of the disappearance.
how_it_feels: Like a movie where the monster comes back. Initially exciting, then suspicious.
what_to_do: They owe you an explanation, not just a casual re-entry. You're allowed to ask 'what happened?' and decide based on the answer.

definition: While in a relationship (or situationship), maintaining a few other flirtatious connections as 'cushions' in case the main thing doesn't work out.
example: He's texting her like she's a priority but is still sliding into DMs on the side — just in case.
how_it_feels: Dishonest. It's not polyamory — it's hedging bets without transparency.
what_to_do: If you're doing it: figure out why you're not confident in your main relationship. If it's being done to you: trust your gut.

definition: When someone keeps you completely separate from their social circle, family, and friends — as if they're hiding you in their pocket.
example: They've been dating for 4 months but he's never mentioned her to his friends and always has excuses for why she can't come to group hangouts.
how_it_feels: Like a secret. And not a fun one.
what_to_do: Ask about it directly. Some people are private — that's fair. But consistent exclusion from their world after months is a conversation worth having.
indian_context: Very common when relationships would be disapproved of by family — religion, caste, or background differences. Context matters.

definition: Similar to pocketing — they're not introducing you to anyone AND actively hiding your relationship from their social media and friends.
example: She's happy in the relationship but notices she's never tagged, never mentioned, and hasn't met a single friend.
how_it_feels: Like existing only in their private messages.
what_to_do: Have a direct conversation. Ask where this is going and whether they're proud of what you have.

definition: When someone makes exciting plans about the future (trips, living together, meeting family) that they never intend to follow through on — using the future as a distraction from present problems.
example: 'We'll go to Goa together next summer.' 'I want to introduce you to my parents eventually.' (Both said 6 months ago. Nothing has happened.)
how_it_feels: Like being handed beautiful gift wrap with nothing inside.
what_to_do: Watch actions, not words. Everyone says nice future-things early on. The question is whether they actually happen.

definition: A manipulation tactic where someone makes you question your own memory, perception, or sanity to avoid accountability.
example: 'That never happened.' 'You're being too sensitive.' 'I never said that.' (When they definitely did.)
how_it_feels: Dizzy. Confused. Like you can't trust your own brain.
what_to_do: Trust your gut. Keep notes if something feels off. Talk to a trusted friend for perspective. This is serious — please reach out to someone you trust.

definition: A mild form of catfishing — using photos from years ago, exaggerating your life, or presenting a slightly altered version of yourself online.
example: His Bumble photo is from 2020 when he was 10kg lighter. His bio says 'entrepreneur' — he sells things occasionally on OLX.
how_it_feels: Annoying when you meet them and reality doesn't match the profile.
what_to_do: Everyone puts their best foot forward online. A little polish is normal. But if someone is deeply misleading, that's a trust issue.
indian_context: Heavily filtered photos and inflated job titles are extremely common on Indian matrimonial apps.

definition: Creating a completely fake online persona — fake photos, fake name, fake life — to deceive someone into a romantic connection.
example: She fell for 'Arjun' for three months before discovering the photos were stolen from a fitness influencer in Dubai.
how_it_feels: Deeply violating and disorienting.
what_to_do: Do a reverse image search. Video call early. If they always have excuses not to video call, be cautious. Trust is earned, not assumed.
indian_context: Catfishing is used in romance scams — financial fraud often follows. Please be careful.

definition: A sudden, visceral feeling of disgust or turn-off triggered by a specific behaviour — even if the person was fine before. Can feel irrational but it's a valid response.
example: He liked her, until he watched her eat soup. Something about the way she slurped it gave him 'the ick' and he couldn't shake it.
how_it_feels: Instantaneous. Like a switch flipping.
what_to_do: Reflect before acting. Is this a genuine incompatibility or just a quirk? Big icks (values, respect) matter. Soup icks might be worth pushing through.

definition: Natural charm and charisma in romantic or social situations. Your ability to attract someone through wit, confidence, and smooth conversation.
example: 'Bro walked up, said two things, and she was already laughing. Man has rizz.'
how_it_feels: Watching someone with rizz is both impressive and slightly intimidating.
what_to_do: Rizz isn't about lines — it's about presence, listening, and being genuinely interested. Good news: it can be developed.

definition: Short for 'delusional.' Believing something about a romantic situation that has no basis in reality — usually wishful thinking cranked to 11.
example: 'She replied to my story with 🔥 — I think she's into me.' (They've never actually spoken.)
how_it_feels: Fun at first. Painful when reality arrives.
what_to_do: Check your evidence. A fire emoji is a fire emoji. Talk to a friend who will be honest with you before going all in.
indian_context: Instagram story reactions are the number one fuel for delulu energy in South Asia.

definition: Someone who is excessively attentive, available, or self-sacrificing for someone who doesn't reciprocate — often losing self-respect in the process.
example: He texts immediately every time, cancels his plans for her, buys things she mentions in passing — and she treats him as an afterthought.
how_it_feels: Exhausting. And the other person rarely respects it.
what_to_do: Caring is great. Over-pursuing someone who doesn't match your energy is not. Have standards for how you deserve to be treated.

definition: Someone who constantly downplays themselves, puts others down, or changes their personality to gain approval from a romantic interest.
example: 'I'm not like other girls — I actually like cricket.' (Said entirely to impress him, not because she genuinely likes cricket.)
how_it_feels: Desperate approval-seeking that usually backfires.
what_to_do: Be yourself. The right person will like the real you. Changing yourself to be liked means being liked for someone you're not.

definition: A warning sign in a person's behaviour or a situation that indicates something potentially harmful, dishonest, or unhealthy.
example: He gets angry when she talks to male friends. She makes all their plans and never considers what he wants. Both red flags.
how_it_feels: Uneasy. Your gut is usually right.
what_to_do: Don't ignore them. One flag might be a bad day. A pattern of flags is information. Pay attention.

definition: A positive sign that someone is emotionally healthy, respectful, and a good potential partner.
example: He listens without interrupting. She's honest when she's not available. He apologises when he's wrong. She respects a 'no'.
how_it_feels: Safe. Calm. Like you can relax.
what_to_do: Notice green flags as much as you notice red ones. It's easy to only look for problems.

definition: A quirk or trait that is neither a red nor green flag — just a bit… boring or weird. Not a dealbreaker, but notable.
example: He replies to every text with exactly one sentence. She talks about her pet fish for 20 minutes. Beige.
how_it_feels: Mildly confusing. You're not alarmed but you're not excited either.
what_to_do: Beige flags are just personality. Can you live with them? That's the question.

definition: The period in late autumn/winter when people feel a stronger urge to be in a relationship — driven by cold weather, holidays, and general cosy-wanting energy.
example: He hadn't thought about dating since summer but now it's December and he's suddenly texting everyone.
how_it_feels: Seasonal loneliness with romantic overtones.
what_to_do: Wanting company in winter is human. Just make sure you actually like the person and not just the warmth they represent.
indian_context: Less seasonal in tropical climates but exam season, hostel loneliness, and festival pressure create similar spikes.

definition: Gradually reducing contact and investment in a relationship until it quietly disappears — without ever having a conversation.
example: Replies went from immediate to same-day to once a week to… never. Nothing dramatic. Just a quiet disappearing act.
how_it_feels: Confusing, because there's no moment to react to. Just a slow fading away.
what_to_do: It's okay to ask 'hey, I've noticed things have been quieter — are we good?' If you get a slow response to that too, you have your answer.

definition: When someone alternates between being very interested and very distant — confusing, unpredictable, and exhausting.
example: Monday: intense texting, making plans. Friday: one-word replies, seems unbothered. Repeat forever.
how_it_feels: Like being on an emotional rollercoaster with no off switch.
what_to_do: This inconsistency is information. Some people genuinely have anxiety — that's worth a conversation. But if it's a pattern, it's draining and you deserve consistency.

definition: Sharing heavy emotional baggage too intensely, too early, or without checking if the other person has the capacity to hold it.
example: On the second date, she shared three deeply traumatic childhood stories without asking if he was okay with heavy conversation.
how_it_feels: Overwhelming. You want to be supportive but it's a lot for early stages.
what_to_do: Vulnerability is beautiful. Trauma dumping is different — it's about pacing. Share when you trust someone, not to test if they'll stay.

definition: A friendship that includes physical intimacy without romantic commitment.
example: They're friends who occasionally hook up, with a mutual understanding of no strings attached.
how_it_feels: Can feel easy and comfortable — until one person catches feelings.
what_to_do: Requires clear, honest communication and regular check-ins. Feelings can change — when they do, the conversation must happen.

definition: Going back to a previous relationship or situationship, often driven by nostalgia, loneliness, or familiarity rather than genuine change.
example: She broke up with him for valid reasons. Six months later she's back, feeling lonely, and 'giving it another chance.'
how_it_feels: Comfortable but risky. Like rewearing a shirt that didn't fit before.
what_to_do: Ask yourself: has anything actually changed? Nostalgic feelings are real but they're not the same as compatibility.

definition: Consciously or unconsciously adopting the personality, interests, or communication style of the person you like to seem more compatible.
example: He starts listening to Radiohead because she does. He starts using her slang. He agrees with everything she says.
how_it_feels: Natural in small doses — it's part of bonding. In excess, it's losing yourself.
what_to_do: Some mirroring is human and healthy. If you're losing your own preferences and opinions completely, pause and reconnect with who you actually are.

definition: When someone is celebrated or considered a 'good partner' for doing things that are just… basic human decency.
example: 'He texts me back the same day.' 'She doesn't lie to me.' These are the minimum, not relationship goals.
how_it_feels: Eye-opening when you realise you've been treating the floor as the ceiling.
what_to_do: Know the difference between effort and the bare minimum. You deserve someone who actively shows up, not just someone who doesn't actively hurt you.

definition: Getting into a new relationship or flirtation quickly after a breakup — often to avoid processing the previous relationship.
example: He broke up with his girlfriend of 2 years and was 'talking to someone new' within 3 weeks.
how_it_feels: Distracting at first. Until the unprocessed feelings catch up.
what_to_do: It's okay to meet new people. But notice if you're running from feelings or genuinely excited about someone new.

definition: When a relationship is publicly confirmed on Instagram — tagged photos, mentions in captions, or being featured in stories.
example: She posted their photo with a ❤️ and tagged him. Before that, they were 'just talking.' Now they're Insta-official.
how_it_feels: Like a public announcement. Exciting but carries weight.
what_to_do: Discuss comfort levels before either person posts. Not everyone is ready for social media visibility at the same time.
indian_context: Going Insta-official in India can alert extended family. Know what you're signing up for.

definition: Excessively showing off or name-dropping achievements, possessions, or social status to impress a romantic interest.
example: 'Oh this? Just my dad's company car.' 'Yeah I'm going to London next month, again.' Said casually but clearly not casually.
how_it_feels: Exhausting to be around. You wonder if the person even exists without the performance.
what_to_do: Everyone wants to impress. Light showing off is normal early on. Relentless showboating suggests insecurity or misaligned values.
indian_context: Family wealth, foreign trips, and 'package' (salary) are common showboating currencies in Indian dating.

definition: A connection that felt like a real relationship in every way — the feelings, the time spent, the intimacy — but never became one.
example: They were inseparable for 6 months. He met her family. She helped him through hard times. But he 'wasn't ready for a relationship.'
how_it_feels: A grief that's hard to explain because others say 'but you weren't even dating.'
what_to_do: The feelings were real even if the label wasn't. It's okay to mourn it. And it's okay to want a relationship next time, not an almost.

definition: Actively dating and keeping options open with multiple people simultaneously — like a sports roster of potential partners.
example: She's talking to four people right now: one from Bumble, one from college, one from work, one who slid into her DMs.
how_it_feels: Empowering when intentional and honest. Messy when feelings get involved.
what_to_do: Dating multiple people is fine before exclusivity is established. Be transparent if someone asks. Once exclusivity is discussed, the roster should close.

definition: A relationship where partners are geographically separated — different cities, states, or countries — and navigate love across distance.
example: She moved to Bangalore for work. He's still in Chennai. They make it work with daily calls and visits every 6 weeks.
how_it_feels: Emotionally rich but logistically demanding. Can be beautiful or exhausting depending on communication.
what_to_do: LDRs need explicit communication about frequency, visits, and an end-goal. 'We'll figure it out' is not a plan.
indian_context: Very common in India due to job transfers, educational migration (BITS, IIT, etc.), and arranged marriage long-distance courtships.

definition: A vague term meaning you're in contact with someone romantically — beyond just texting as friends, but not yet in a relationship.
example: 'Are you dating anyone?' 'No, but I'm… talking to someone.' (Significant pause and possible blush.)
how_it_feels: Hopeful and undefined.
what_to_do: The talking stage is real but it shouldn't last forever. If things are going well, move toward clarity.

definition: Instagram's feature that limits who sees a story — and the social meaning around who gets added or removed.
example: She added him to her Close Friends list. He took a screenshot and sent it to his friends with 27 fire emojis.
how_it_feels: Exclusive. Slightly giddy.
what_to_do: Being added to Close Friends is a signal of trust and interest. Being removed is worth a light check-in if things have been tense.
indian_context: In India, the Close Friends list is a serious social currency — sometimes more meaningful than a follow.

definition: A relationship that develops in the unique pressure-cooker environment of college — intense, accelerated, and often complicated by proximity.
example: They met in their first-year dorm, fell hard, spent every day together — and then graduation pulled them in different directions.
how_it_feels: Incredibly intense. College time is compressed and feelings match that pace.
what_to_do: Enjoy it fully. But be intentional about what happens when college ends — talk about it rather than assuming.
indian_context: College romances in India often operate in secrecy from families, which adds pressure and drama.

definition: External pressure from family members to date or marry a certain type of person, within a certain timeline, or not date at all.
example: 'She's the right age, from a good family, well-settled. When are you asking?' — from a parent who doesn't know you're not even officially dating yet.
how_it_feels: Stifling. Like your personal relationship is actually a family group project.
what_to_do: Family input is real and sometimes valid. But YOUR life needs to be lived by YOU. It's okay to set gentle boundaries around what you share.
indian_context: Unique and intense in South Asian contexts — caste, religion, horoscope, and 'settling down age' are all factors.
